Free from such limitations, classical molecular simulations, in the general frameworks of Monte Carlo and Molecular Dynamics, provide an optimal balance between computational efficiency and accuracy, bridging the gap between quantum mechanical calculations and macro-scale modeling. This review also systematically covers molecular simulation methods and force fields for computing key properties of H<sub>2</sub> systems, such as phase and adsorption equilibria and transport coefficients. Beyond property prediction, we explore how molecular simulation reveals fundamental mechanisms governing hydrate formation and dissociation, membrane permeations, and H<sub>2</sub> embrittlement.
